lawRefs: 68 O.S. § 2355 as amended by 2025 HB 2764 (three brackets, 4.5% top rate from tax year 2026; revenue-triggered future 0.25-point cuts)
68 O.S. § 2358 (standard deduction, $1,000 exemption, retirement and Social Security exclusions)
header.notes: sha256 is of the canonical JSON body (JSON.stringify of the file without `header`). Hand-transcribed; sha256 is of the canonical body. Brackets derived from the OTC 2026 Income Tax Withholding Tables (Packet OW-2) annual percentage formula, which embeds the standard deduction (single: 0% to $10,100 = $6,350 + $3,750, then 2.5% to $11,250, 3.5% to $13,550, 4.5% above; married: $20,200 / $22,500 / $27,100), and they match HB 2764 and Tax Foundation 2026. Statutory taxable-income brackets: 0% on the first $3,750 ($7,500 MFJ), 2.5% to $4,900 ($9,800), 3.5% to $7,200 ($14,400), 4.5% above. Head of household and surviving spouse use the MFJ schedule; MFS uses the single schedule. Standard deduction $6,350 single/MFS, $12,700 MFJ, $9,350 HOH (fixed, not indexed). Personal exemption $1,000 per person including dependents (an extra $1,000 for 65+ only at federal AGI <= $15,000 single / $25,000 joint). Social Security benefits included in federal AGI are fully subtracted. Retirement exclusion: up to $10,000 per person of benefits from 401/403/457 plans, IRAs/SEPs and Oklahoma or federal civil-service pensions, no age requirement (early distributions on termination before retirement do not qualify for the government-plan line); CSRS in lieu of Social Security and military retirement are 100% exempt. No rate trigger has taken effect for 2026 (earliest possible is tax year 2028).

flags.retirementIncomeExclusion: simplified: 10,000 combined cap across government and private plans; no statutory minimum age
